items.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
I am looking for a flat.
Could I get the check, please?
We would like to pay together.
Is this the queue for boarding?

items.tr: 저 gibi ünlü ile biten kelimelerden sonra 는 gelir, ünsüzle bitenlerden sonra 은 gelir.
items.en: 는 follows a word ending in a vowel (like 저), and 은 follows a word ending in a consonant.
A stranger smiles and greets you.
You want to know their name too.
You are curious where they are from.
They ask where you are from.
You want to know their job.
What do you do for work?

items.tr: 을/를 fiilin nesnesini işaretler; ünsüzle biten kelimeden sonra 을, ünlüyle bitenden sonra 를 gelir.
items.en: 을/를 marks the object of the verb: 을 after a consonant-ending word, 를 after a vowel-ending one.
You are looking at a shirt.
You want to try it on.
Excuse me, do you have another color?
Do you have a smaller size?

items.tr: Belirli bir saati söylerken 에 eklenir ("...de/da" anlamında).
items.en: 에 attaches to a specific clock time to mean 'at ___'.
items.context: 일곱 시에 만나요. / ✗ 일곱 시가 만나요.

items.en: You are planning to meet a friend.
The cashier tells you the total.
What time does the train leave?
Let's meet at seven in the evening.

items.tr: Aile üyelerini sayarken sayı ile isim arasına "명" (kişi sayaç kelimesi) gelir.
items.en: When counting family members, put the counter word 명 between the number and the noun.
items.context: 오빠가 한 명 있어요. / ✗ 오빠가 한 있어요.

items.en: You ask them the same question.
They ask your place in the family.
They ask who else lives with you.
My dad works at a hospital.
I'm the youngest in the family.

items.tr: ㅂ ile biten bazı sıfatlar (춥다 gibi) çekimlenirken ㅂ düşer ve 워 eklenir.
items.en: Some adjectives ending in ㅂ (like 춥다, 'cold') drop the ㅂ and add 워 when conjugated.
A friend is leaving without a coat.
They ask about your favorite weather.
Take an umbrella, it might rain.

items.tr: Bir ulaşım aracına binmeyi anlatmak için araç adından sonra 을/를 gelir, sonra 타다 fiili kullanılır.
items.en: To say you take a vehicle, mark it with 을/를 and use the verb 타다 (to ride).
They ask how you get to work.
You are at the ticket counter.
You want to catch the last train.
A friend offers you a ride.
Excuse me, how do I get downtown?
I take the bus to work.
Does this bus go to the airport?
One ticket to the central station, please.
What time does the last train leave?

items.tr: Bir şeyi rica etmek için fiil gövdesine 아/어 주세요 eklenir, çekimli hale değil.
items.en: To make a polite request, add 아/어 주세요 to the verb stem, not to its already-conjugated form.

items.tr: 동사 어간 + 고 나서, "yaptıktan sonra" sırasını anlatır.
items.en: Verb stem + 고 나서 shows the order of actions: 'after doing ___'.
items.context: 먹고 나서 봐요. / ✗ 먹어서 나서 봐요.

items.en: They ask how you get to work.
They ask when your day ends.
I get up at seven every day.
I brush my teeth, then take a shower.
I go to work by bike.
I finish work at six in the evening.
After eating dinner, I watch TV.
I go to bed at eleven.

items.tr: Geçmiş zaman için fiil/sıfat gövdesine (ünlü uyumuna göre) 았/었어요 eklenir.
items.en: For the past tense, add 았/었어요 to the verb/adjective stem, following vowel harmony.
items.context: 어제 공항에 갔어요. / ✗ 어제 공항에 가요.

items.en: They ask about your day yesterday.
They ask what you did together.
They ask when you got home.
They ask how your day was.
Yesterday I went to the airport.
I met an old friend there.
I finally arrived home at midnight.
Ask for the next place or step.
Excuse me, where is the station?
Say what you did not understand.
Describe what you are looking for.
Ask about the cost or condition.
I am looking for a flat.

items.target: 저녁에 민준이 집에 왔고, 우리는 차를 마셨습니다.
items.tr: Akşam Minjun bana geldi, çay içtik.
Arkadaşıma telefon edip yürüyüşe çıkmayı teklif ettim.

items.target: 저는 목록을 가지고 가서 아무것도 잊지 않았습니다.
items.tr: Listemi alıp gittim, hiçbir şeyi unutmadım.
Eve dönüp lezzetli bir kahvaltı hazırladım.
